name: Update Tile Entity
desc: Updates NBT data for a tile entity (sign, skull, beacon, command block, etc.).

writeup.p: Server-pushed NBT updates for tile entities: a BlockPos, a one-byte action type, and an NBT tag. The action discriminates the tile entity class (1 mob spawner, 2 command block, 3 beacon, 4 skull, 5 flower pot, 6 banner), and the client applies the tag only when the loaded tile entity at that position matches the action. It is the per-block complement to the block change packets: S22 and S23 carry block ids and metadata, while S35 carries the full compound for the entity attached to a block. Sign line edits, skull owner changes, beacon effect retunes and spawner entity swaps all arrive here.

NetHandlerPlayClient.handleUpdateTileEntity dispatches on the main thread (PacketThreadUtil), checks isBlockLoaded(pos), fetches the tile entity, and calls readFromNBT only when the action matches the tile entity class; an unloaded position or a mismatched type is silently dropped, so a forged packet cannot create tile entities out of thin air. The producers are the tile entities themselves: TileEntityMobSpawner emits action 1, TileEntityCommandBlock 2, TileEntityBeacon 3, TileEntitySkull 4, TileEntityFlowerPot 5, TileEntityBanner 6.

In this corpus they do not. The mined grep across all 8 clients returns only the vanilla handler, the EnumConnectionState registration, the INetHandlerPlayClient declaration and the tile entity producers; the only non-vanilla hit is Rise 6.1.30 and 6.2.4 NetworkAPI.java registering S35PacketUpdateTileEntity.class for the script engine. There is no SignESP, chest tracker or beacon ESP module referencing S35 in Memeware, Nekoware, Rise, Sigma, Spicy or Tenacity. The metadata drafts for Tenacity 6.0 ChestESP and SpawnerFinder fail corpus verification and are deliberately not listed.

Because the handler requires a loaded chunk and a matching tile entity class, the packet is a poor injection surface and no anti-cheat measures it. The realistic module use would be read-only: sniffing sign text players type, or tracking spawner and beacon changes for ESP. Their absence in these clients is a corpus fact rather than a protocol limitation; nothing about the wire format stops a client from observing the stream.

implementation.overview: The tile entity state channel: the server pushes NBT diffs for signs, spawners, command blocks, beacons, skulls, flower pots and banners, and the client applies them only when the loaded tile entity matches the action byte. None of the 8 clients ships a module that reads or cancels this packet; the corpus holds only vanilla handler and producer hits plus Rise 6.x script API registration.
implementation.server_handling: The server never validates the payload beyond construction: each tile entity builds its own packet from its NBT via getUpdatePacket, and the server sends it to the relevant players. The readFromNBT gate on the client is the only enforcement point. The action byte is read as unsigned, so the vanilla set of 1-6 is a convention rather than a wire constraint; modded servers reuse the channel for custom tile entities.
implementation.protocol_notes: Wire layout: BlockPos (a packed long, x << 38 | z << 12 | y in the 1.8.9 encoding), an unsigned byte action, then a length-prefixed NBT compound. The NBT payload dominates the size: a banner pattern list or a long command block command can push the packet past the server compression threshold. Frequent beacon or spawner updates are a known bandwidth cost on chunk-heavy servers.
implementation.anticheat_landscape: No anti-cheat watches S35; it is server-trusted data flowing clientbound. The only abuse vector is a malicious server shipping crafted NBT to crash or lag clients, which is a server-side concern outside module scope. Clients gain nothing by spoofing it because the direction is clientbound and the handler discards mismatches, so the packet contributes nothing to detection or evasion.
implementation.general_hooks: The natural hook surface is PacketReceiveEvent, but no module in the 8-client corpus registers one for S35; Rise 6.x additionally exposes the class through its script NetworkAPI whitelist.
implementation.client_variations: Rise 6.1.30 and 6.2.4 let scripts match S35 through the script API packet registry; the other six clients carry only vanilla references.

anticheat.overview: No anti-cheat consumes S35. Every corpus hit matches the TileEntity keyword rather than the packet: Grim's chunk readers and CompensatedWorld pass TileEntity arrays embedded in map-chunk data, NCP's BlockCache implementations call world.getTileEntity to read server-side block state, Kauri's BlockUpdateHandler forwards the same chunk-embedded array, Photon's WorldDownloaderSentinel writes a disable-tile-entity-saving option into the WorldDownloader channel, and intave's EntityTypeDataRegistry is a misnamed entity-type hitbox table. The only direct packet references are plumbing: Negativity's TILE_ENTITY_DATA constant, and Artemis' PacketRepository entry with the PacketPlayServerTileEntityData wrapper interface. Tile-entity policing runs on the commit side of sign edits instead: NCP AutoSign and Intave ItemCrashTracker.checkSign watch C12PacketUpdateSign, because S35 is server-trusted NBT the client applies only when the loaded tile entity matches the action byte.
